title: Missing the plane to Paris and Duke wanting to know what happened in Brussels
summary: Jones finishes the story of meeting his wife in Paris, her "I caught you again", and Duke asking about it from his hospital bed.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, yes. Okay. We'd had a nice time -- I'm speaking about Mercer and his son, young Edward, and myself, and we missed the morning plane going into Paris, and so fortunately we didn't have to work that night, but I was supposed to -- I had an appointment with my wife. She'd never been to Paris, you know, she'd never flown over all that water, and she was really cute. She cried, and when we got to the hotel, oh, Johnny Griffin, Ben Webster, Jimmy Wood$, the bass player that was formerly with Duke, and who else -- Jill Hughes, Joe Williams's wife's cousin, was there, you know. And Johnny Hodges' wife was there, you know. So just to back up on that story. This has to be -- of course now my wife and I, we travelled and we had a beautiful time. Went to Spain, London, you know, Germany, and another thing that backed up on it that was quite funny, the year before we played the Riviera in South France, you know, and so we were staying on Half Moon Street, right there in the Picadilly Circus area, in the hotel, and my wife were getting ready to just go out to the theater or something, you know? We had some time off. And so two of the girls from the Riviera came to the desk and says, 'Is Jimmy Jones here?' And they were twins, you know? And my wife was just sitting in the lobby, and so the guy on the desk says,

"He's upstairs, but you can speak to his wife over there." So when I came downstairs, boy, she was swollen up as big as an elephant. The chicks had gone by then, you know. I said, "Baby, what's the matter?" And, you know, just had her jaw stuck out. We went to every theater, I guess I spent my whole salary on her that week, buying clothes, trying to -- and she broke up laughing. She said, "I caught you again, didn't I?" (Laughter)

And I'd spent up all my money. But we just went all over the place, you know. So this is the backup on the Ellington I wanted to give you. His grandson -- he was working with his son Mercer when they had the band in Dantes, I guess it was last year or so.
A couple of years ago, I think.

Yeah, I guess so. And he says, "You know what my grandfather said?" Now, Duke is in the hospital on his last bed. He said, -- young Edward, he says, "I've figured out everything else as much as I could go, but I could never figure out what happened with you, Jimmy Jones and Mercer in Brussels." I said, "Well, Edward, your grandfather was one of a kind. He would be the only one that would do something like that." He's getting ready to shake hands with the judge and he's trying to figure out what happened to us in Brussels.
Well, he always wanted to know everybody's business, you know.
He couldn't stand to have something go on that he didn't know about or plan or influence or something. Now you did that and he didn't choreograph it.
Uh-huh. But that was funny. He said, 'I just wanted to know what happened to Jimmy Jones and you in Brussels.'
I know Edward didn't tell him, did he?

I don't think he did. Glad I wasn't there, you know? But Duke knew that Speedy was due in, you know, in Paris, because he couldn't figure out what I was doing in Brussels and my wife's coming to Paris, you know?
Oh, gee, that was about '60 -- in the middle '60s.
Let's see, I came out here permanently in '67 and this should have been maybe '65, somewhere around there you know.
